verdicts.reason: I could not refute this claim. At 36ea5db the time series are thinned twice by keeping every Nth row, and nothing preserves the peaks. First, loader.py:267-273 and 316-319 keep every Nth row with the target set to report_pts*4. Then html_report.py:193-236 thins the same series again with range(0, len, len//ts_pts). Only the scalar peak_* fields keep the true peak. The JavaScript KPIs work from the thinned series: Impact Phase Timing Peak G and time to peak, computePulseMetrics (peak, pulse width, impulse, half-sine), the hot-spot and critical element tables (elems[maxIdx]), Crack Arrest peakStress and the Time History charts. None of these carry a note that the data is downsampled. The path is production: koo_sphere_report ships in SmartTwinPostprocessor.def, and --ts-points defaults to 0, which picks the adaptive tier. I reran the snapshot's own loader functions plus the HTML stride on the real campaign /data/Tests/Test_006_Fibonacci_6deg (1144 runs, 993-row CSVs). Each series drops to 42 points after the loader and 11 in the HTML. The G series in the HTML shows a median of 37% of the true peak, and stress shows 80%. The worst stress case matches the claim exactly: Run_20260207_215839_edb467 part 14 has a true peak of 227.63 that shows as 61.5. report.json (json_report.py:110-133) gets the same stride. A kg-mm-ms deck (density 7.85e-6) is even detected as ton-mm-s, so a GPa report would be wrong for reasons that have nothing to do with rounding. In real payloads peak_stress is 13.6 to 10935 MPa, so 1 or 2 decimals lose nothing that matters, and time at 6 or 7 decimals in seconds is fine once the series is cut to 10 to 100 points.

confirmed.mechanism: `for mk in ("g", "s", "e", "d"):` builds Sample.metrics; the other METRIC_KEYS are absent, so compare.scaled returns None, `complete=False`, and gate reason is `"값 없음: " + label`.
confirmed.scenario: Snapshot run: two sphere sidecars with 100 Fibonacci angles, B offset by 3° pitch, every cell carrying peak_principal_stress 250. `resample: idw` gives metric s n_comparable 100/100 but metric s1 n_comparable 0/100 with gate_reason '값 없음: B', although B has s1 at every angle.
confirmed.consumers: Federate report with options.resample: idw and --metric s1|s3|e1|e3|evm: all Δ maps, profile, parts table (gated) and no_comparable_cells ERROR blaming the data.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Iterate over models.METRIC_KEYS in _idw_sample. For compressive metrics interpolate the signed value; do not report interpolation gaps as '값 없음'.

verdicts.reason:
The claim holds. At 36ea5db, `_idw_sample` (resample.py:279) fills in only g, s, e and d. `models.METRIC_KEYS` has 9 keys, and the CLI `--metric` accepts all 9. The sphere adapter does load s1, s3, e1, e3 and evm from the sidecar (peak_principal_stress and the others), and koo_sphere_report's json_report and html_report write those fields.

When a grid node gets an IDW sample, that sample has none of the other five metrics. `compare.scaled` returns None for them, so `complete=False`. The cell is gated with the reason '값 없음: <rev>', even though every revision has that metric at every angle.

I rebuilt the claim's scenario from the package as of 36ea5db: two sphere sidecars with 100 Fibonacci angles each, B shifted 3 degrees in pitch, `resample: idw`. Results:
- metric s: 100/100 cells comparable.
- metrics s1, s3 and evm: 0/100 comparable, every gate_reason is '값 없음: B', the `no_comparable_cells` ERROR is raised, and the parts table shows worst=[None, None] with status gated.

Only nodes where every revision matches exactly keep all metrics. When the angle grids differ, the IDW Fibonacci nodes almost never line up exactly with measured angles, so in practice every interpolated cell is affected.

This is reachable in production through the koo_federate_report CLI shipped in the SIF (build_module.sh wrapper, SmartTwinPostprocessor.def). It needs two non-default settings: `options.resample: idw` (the default is nearest) and a principal or von Mises `--metric` (the default is g).

The result is a loud but misattributed loss: every Δ map, trend and part-table value for that metric is dropped, and the error blames missing data. No wrong number is shown. I rate it medium.

The claim holds; I reproduced it with the code exported from commit 36ea5db. In `resample._idw_sample`, lines 279-289 build `metrics` only for "g", "s", "e" and "d". `models.METRIC_KEYS` (models.py:22) also has s1, s3, e1, e3 and evm, and `adapters/sphere.py` (lines 22-24, 90-94) fills those five from the sidecar's peak_principal_stress, min_principal_stress, peak_principal_strain, min_principal_strain and peak_vm_strain. koo_sphere_report writes those fields (html_report.py:173-182). Every cell that IDW fills therefore has s1/s3/e1/e3/evm set to None, not interpolated. In `compare.build_comparison`, `scaled()` then returns None, so `complete` is False, the cell is gated with the reason "값 없음: <rev>", and it counts as not comparable. When all cells are interpolated, the ERROR `no_comparable_cells` fires. The parts table uses `cell["gated"]`, so every part gets `worst=None` with data_status 'gated'. The report blames missing data even though every revision has the metric at every angle. Reaching this in production needs several less common choices: `options.resample: idw` (the default is nearest), `--metric` set to one of the five principal or von Mises strain metrics, and revisions whose angle grids differ (identical keys take the identity path). The failure is loud, not a silently wrong number: the ERROR warning fires, but its message blames the data. Medium severity is right.

confirmed.title: --from-json regeneration fabricates 2-point waveforms, drops σ1/σ3/ε/energy, and uses the stress peak time for strain
confirmed.mechanism: `_make_stress_ts`: `times=[0.0, peak_time], max_values=[0.0, peak], avg_values=[0.0, peak]`; `_make_motion`: `mo.avg_acc_mag = [0.0, gval]` with `t = peak_g_time if peak_g_time > 0 else 0.001`. 174-177 strain uses `pd.get("time_of_peak_stress", 0.001)`. peak_principal_stress, min_principal_stress, *_strain, energy, stress_ts/g_ts and tool_builds in report.json are never read.
confirmed.scenario: Snapshot round trip: report.json keys include min_principal_stress, peak_principal_stress, energy, stress_ts, g_ts. The regenerated payload has none of the principal/energy keys. stress_ts becomes {'t': [0.0, 0.00037], 'max': [0.0, 300.0], 'avg': [0.0, 300.0]} (avg = peak is invented) and g_ts becomes {'t': [0.0, 0.0003], 'g': [0.0, 5096.8]}. Strain peak_time is 0.00037 instead of 0.00151. Time History draws a straight ramp, Impact Pulse computes width/impulse from 2 points, Crack Arrest SCF becomes 1.0, and σ1/σ3 columns disappear.
confirmed.consumers: koo_sphere_report CLI `--from-json` → report.html (all time-series tabs, Part Risk principal/energy columns, build note).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Load the stored stress_ts/strain_ts/g_ts/disp_ts, principal, strain and energy keys. If a series is absent, leave it empty and hide the dependent sections instead of synthesizing [0, peak]. Use each quantity's own peak time.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute this claim. At 36ea5db, `from_json.py` rebuilds every time series from peak scalars alone. Stress and strain become the 2 points [0, peak_time] and [0, peak], avg is set equal to max, and acceleration becomes [0, peak_g*G]. The strain series takes its time from `time_of_peak_stress`. The file never reads `stress_ts`, `strain_ts`, `g_ts` or `disp_ts`, nor `peak_principal_stress`, `min_principal_stress`, `peak_*_strain` or `energy`, even though `json_report.save_json` writes all of them. `html_report` then sends these invented series to the time-history, impact-pulse and crack-arrest code. Pulse width and impulse come from a 2-point ramp, and SCF comes out as `peak/avg` = exactly 1.0. Nothing in the HTML says the curves are synthetic.

I ran a round trip on the code as of 36ea5db, extracted to my scratchpad, and got exactly the result the claim describes. The principal-stress, strain and energy values are dropped (None), so those columns vanish.

How it is reached: `--from-json` is a documented CLI mode (docs/Reports_Usage.md). `koo_sphere_report` is built into the SmartTwinPostprocessor SIF, and the shipped `examples/bundle/RUN_TESTS.sh` step 2 uses this mode to rebuild the 1144-angle report. The automated `post_analyze.sh` uses `--test-dir` instead, so only a user who runs the regeneration command hits this.

One small error in the claim: `json_report.py` never writes `tool_builds`, so its not being read loses nothing. That does not affect the main defect. Severity is medium, because the path is production but runs only when a user asks for it.

The defect is real, and I reproduced it by saving a report and reloading it with the code at 36ea5db. `save_json` writes real series (`stress_ts`, `strain_ts`, `g_ts`, `disp_ts`, about 100 points each), σ1/σ3 values and `energy`. `load_report_from_json` never reads any of those keys. Instead it builds made-up 2-point series from the peak values: [0, peak], with avg set equal to peak. It also uses `time_of_peak_stress` as the strain peak time.

The regenerated HTML then shows wrong numbers as if they were measured:
- Impact Pulse gives pulse width 0.000 ms and impulse 0 (the real run gives 0.16 ms and 6.1e-4 MG·ms).
- Energy Absorption gives 1.8 instead of 0.119, about 15x too high, because avg stress is set to peak.
- `peak_vel` is written as 0.0 mm/s, because motion.times is not empty but `avg_vel_mag` is. It shows in the tooltip, the Mollweide velocity map and the velocity-stress scatter.
- `disp_ts.mag` is empty.
- Time History draws a straight ramp.
- Strain peaks at 0.00037 s instead of 0.00151 s.
- The σ1/σ3 and energy keys are missing from the regenerated report.

Two parts of the claim are wrong. First, Crack Arrest does not show SCF=1.0: `buildCrackArrest` has `if (n < 3) continue;`, so it quietly leaves out the whole section. Second, `tool_builds` is never written by `save_json`, so from_json has nothing to read there.

On reach: `--from-json` is a documented CLI mode (docs/Reports_Usage.md:220) in the deployed SIF `koo_sphere_report` command, and examples/bundle/RUN_TESTS.sh uses it. No automated pipeline calls it (post_analyze uses `--test-dir`), and `report.json` is only written with `--format json`. That makes it reachable in production only when a user runs it by hand, so medium severity fits.

confirmed.title: Sphere unit detection maps every ms-based deck to ton-mm-s (or keeps it as default), so peak G is 1e6× too small
confirmed.mechanism: `preset = _detect_unit_system(density)`; `gf = _G_FACTOR_BY_UNIT.get(uid)`; if uid is unknown it keeps `MotionData.G_FACTOR = 9810`. koo_impact_report/loader.py:1011 `if density <= 1.0e-5: return _UNIT_PRESETS["ton-mm-s"]` and 1016 `return _UNIT_UNKNOWN`, so the 'ton-mm-ms'/'g-mm-ms' entries in _G_FACTOR_BY_UNIT (88-89) can never be selected. The only signal is a stdout print.
confirmed.scenario: Snapshot detector: ton-mm-ms steel ρ=7.85e-9 is detected as 'ton-mm-s' (G_FACTOR 9806.65); kg-mm-ms ρ=7.85e-6 is also 'ton-mm-s'; g-mm-ms ρ=7.85e-3 is '' and falls back to 9810. A true 150,000 G peak (acc in mm/ms²) is reported as 0.15 G. The HTML shows 0.00 MG and analyzer's `worst_g > 50000` finding never fires.
confirmed.consumers: peak_g/true_peak_g, g_ts/acc_ts in HTML and report.json, analyzer CRITICAL/WARNING G findings, federate metric g.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Disambiguate time/mass units with more than density (e.g. analysis_result.json end_time magnitude or the deck's *CONTROL_TERMINATION, impact velocity from drop height). When undetermined, mark peak_g as unit-unknown in the payload and HTML instead of silently applying 9810.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute this. The mechanism is real at 36ea5db. The sphere loader works out the unit system from the median *MAT density alone. The impact detector it calls can only return 'ton-mm-s', 'SI' or unknown, so the 'ton-mm-ms' and 'g-mm-ms' entries in _G_FACTOR_BY_UNIT can never be picked. Density cannot tell seconds from milliseconds, so ms-based decks get the wrong G factor.
- **kg-mm-ms** (ρ=7.85e-6): falls under the `<= 1e-5` rule and is reported as 'ton-mm-s'. The log line is the normal "단위계 확인" message, not a warning.
- **g-mm-ms** (ρ=7.85e-3): comes back unknown and keeps the default 9810. MotionData.UNIT_SYSTEM stays "ton-mm-s", so report.json still says ton-mm-s with g_factor 9810 instead of marking it undetected.

In both cases acceleration is in mm/ms², so peak_g, g_series and the analyzer's `worst_g > 50000` finding come out 1e6 times too small. I reproduced this by running the actual detector code from 36ea5db (output below).

Why medium and not high: every campaign on this machine is ton-mm-s. The median density of all 165 runner decks I sampled is between 2e-9 and 7.85e-9, and runner_config tFinal is 0.001-0.005 s. The pyKooCAE runner only auto-detects ton-mm-s and kg-m-s. It does accept an explicit "Gravity" option, so a user with a kg-mm-ms or g-mm-ms model can still produce a consistent ms deck that this report then reads. That makes it a production path that needs less common input. It is also not a regression: before commit 8ad56a9 the factor was hard-coded to 9810, which was just as wrong for ms decks.

The mechanism is real, but the scenario can't happen with the inputs this pipeline produces. At 36ea5db, sphere calls `_detect_unit_system(density)` with density only, and that function never returns 'ton-mm-ms' or 'g-mm-ms'. A ton-mm-ms deck has exactly the same density as a ton-mm-s deck, so density alone can never tell them apart. The claim's numbers reproduce: a true 150,000 G peak in mm/ms² would show as 0.15 G.

Why it doesn't reach production:
(1) The DOE runner that builds every sphere run assumes mm with time in seconds. Its drop velocity is v0 = sqrt(2·9810·h), which gives 5425 for h=1500 (units mm/s), and ENDTIM is 1e-3 or 5e-3 s. A deck in ms units run through this pipeline would already be a wrong simulation (a drop at 5.4 km/s) before any report is built.
(2) I checked all 59 test folders on /data that have a runner_config.json. The median *MAT density in every one is 2e-9 to 7.85e-9 (ton-mm-s). None uses ms units.
(3) This is not a regression: before the detector existed, G_FACTOR was hard-coded to 9810 (ton-mm-s). For an ms deck, the detector gives the same answer as the old code.
The ms-deck issue stays as a low-severity latent limit.

A separate defect in the same function does happen on real data. `_deck_density` splits each *MAT line on whitespace. In fixed-width cards where MID runs into RO (e.g. `232.33000E-9  166000.0`), it reads E as the density. On two real ton-mm-s decks it switches the report to SI (G_FACTOR 9.80665), so peak G comes out 1000× too large. This should be filed as its own finding.

confirmed.title: Sphere sidecars get hard-coded MPa/mm/G unit labels, so the federate unit-mismatch guard can never fire for sphere revisions
confirmed.mechanism: `unit_labels=dict(raw.get("unit_labels") or _SPHERE_DEFAULT_UNITS)` where `_SPHERE_DEFAULT_UNITS = {"acc": "G", "stress": "MPa", "disp": "mm", ...}` (31-40). json_report.py never writes unit_labels or the detected unit system. compare.py:_unit_factors (234-236) sees identical labels and returns factor 1.0 with no warning, even under unit_policy 'error'.
confirmed.scenario: Revision A from an SI deck (stress Pa: peak 3.1e8, disp m: 0.012) vs revision B from a ton-mm-s deck (310 MPa, 12 mm). Both are labeled MPa/mm, so federate reports stress Δ% = -99.9999% and disp Δ% = -99.9% as real improvements with no unit_converted/unit_unknown warning.
confirmed.consumers: Federate Δ/trend/winner/parts for metrics s, s1, s3, d (and e unaffected); KPI table unit captions.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Have koo_sphere_report json_report write unit_labels from the detected unit system (MotionData.UNIT_SYSTEM plus the impact presets). In the adapter, leave labels empty when absent so the guard can warn about unknown units instead of inventing MPa/mm.

verdicts.reason:
The defect is real, and I reproduced it on the code at 36ea5db. Sphere report.json files never record units. `json_report.save_json` writes no `unit_labels` and no unit system. The HTML report does store `unit_system`, but that value never reaches the sidecar. The sphere loader already handles SI decks: `_apply_unit_system` detects SI from the deck density. However, only peak_g is converted, from acceleration to G. peak_stress and peak_disp stay in the deck's own units, so an SI deck gives Pa and m.

When `raw['unit_labels']` is missing, the federate sphere adapter fills in `_SPHERE_DEFAULT_UNITS` (MPa/mm). `_unit_factors` then sees the same labels on every revision and skips them (`if not lb or not li or lb == li: continue`). The factor stays 1.0, no warning is added, and no CompareError is raised, even under `unit_policy: error`. That is the setting in the shipped example `federate_sphere.yaml`.

One correction to the claim: its scenario gets the displacement sign wrong. With the SI revision as baseline, stress Δ% is -99.9999% and displacement Δ% is +99,900%, not -99.9%. The mechanism is unaffected. Even with a single SI revision, the KPI and table captions show "MPa" next to Pa values such as 3.1e8, because `compare.py:851` passes the baseline's `unit_labels` to `html_report`.

The acceleration metric (g) is unaffected, because sphere stores peak_g in G. Strain has no unit label, so it is unaffected too. Severity is medium. The path runs in production (federate is deployed in the SIF, and the sphere loader explicitly supports SI decks), but it only triggers for sphere DOEs run from SI decks, or when revisions mix unit systems.

The claim holds, and I reproduced it end to end at 36ea5db. koo_sphere_report's json_report.save_json never writes `unit_labels` or the unit system it detects. The sphere loader does detect SI, ton-mm-s and other systems from deck density, but it only uses the result to change G_FACTOR. peak_stress and peak_disp keep the deck's own units (Pa and m for an SI deck).

The federate sphere adapter fills in MPa/mm/G for every sphere sidecar. Because every sphere revision gets the same labels, compare._unit_factors takes the `lb == li` branch, returns factor 1.0 and adds no warning. That holds even under unit_policy: error, which is the shipped default and is what examples/federate_sphere.yaml sets.

The impact adapter is different: impact sidecars carry detected labels (Pa/m for SI), so the guard does work there. Sphere is the one kind where it can never fire.

One correction to the claim: with the SI revision as baseline, the disp Δ% comes out +99900% (reported as much worse), not -99.9%. The mechanism is the same. Even a comparison of SI decks alone is affected: the report shows 3.1e8 labeled "MPa" and 0.012 labeled "mm".

The path is reachable in production, since koo_federate_report is deployed in the SIF and accepts kind sphere/auto. It needs revisions with different unit systems, or an SI sphere deck. That is less common, but the sphere loader's SI detection was added because SI decks do occur. I keep severity at medium.

low.title: set_reports block in analysis_result.json embeds name/title/notes/note without escaping, and set peaks inherit a sticky std::fixed
low.mechanism: `extra << "\n    {\"name\": \"" << sr.name << "\"" ... << ", \"title\": \"" << sr.title << "\""` (806-809), `extra << "\"" << sr.notes[j] << "\""` (823), `", \"note\": \"" << f.note << "\""` (838). Notes include user text such as `"이름 패턴 '" + pat + "' 에 맞는 파트 없음"` (UnifiedAnalyzer.cpp:1157) and renderer error strings (UnifiedAnalyzerSectionRender.cpp:299). metrics.json (unified_analyzer.cpp:362-432) escapes the same strings with jesc; this block does not. Also, `std::setprecision(8)` at 832 inherits std::fixed only when motion/quality/beam sections were non-empty, so set peak formatting depends on unrelated sections.
low.scenario: Reproduced: title `Front\Metal "A"` (the SetReportSpec comment's own pattern example `Front\\Metal`) makes toExtendedJSON emit `"title": "Front\Metal "A""`, and json.loads raises 'Invalid \escape'. A *SET_PART_LIST_TITLE title containing a quote or backslash, or an unmatched YAML part_patterns entry containing a backslash, breaks the custom-report run's analysis_result.json.
low.consumers: The custom_report/<run>/analysis_result.json written by koo_custom_report runs. The Python custom/sphere/impact report code reads set_reports/<set>/metrics.json, not this file, so no current Python consumer breaks. The defect is latent for any tool that reads analysis_result.json from that folder.
low.suggested_fix: Use escapeJSON/jesc for every string in toExtendedJSON (set_reports name/title/notes/note, surface_strain description/note, motion/element_quality part_name) and jnum for the peak values.

low.title: beam_analysis and motion_analysis JSON summaries use fixed(6): peak times 1.5e-7 and 1.4e-7 both print as 0.000000, and small SI displacements/velocities print as 0
low.mechanism: beam: `<< ", \"peak_max\": " << std::fixed << std::setprecision(6) << gmax << ", \"peak_max_time\": " << t_max` (791-796). motion: `<< ", \"peak_velocity\": " << std::fixed << std::setprecision(6) << m.peak_velocity_magnitude << ", \"peak_acceleration\": " ... << ", \"max_displacement\": "` (724-726). BeamAnalyzer.cpp:122-129 leaves tp.max_value/min_value at 0.0 when every beam value in a state is non-finite (deleted), so peak_max can report a placeholder 0 for compression-only beams.
low.scenario: Reproduced: beam points at t=1.5e-7 (max 12.0) and t=1.4e-7 give `peak_max_time 0.0`. A motion point with avg velocity 4e-7 and max displacement 3e-7 (SI m/s, m) gives peak_velocity 0.0 and max_displacement 0.0.
low.consumers: No Python consumer reads beam_analysis or motion_analysis from JSON (the deep/sphere/impact reports use motion CSVs, and beam output is unused), so the defect is latent.
low.suggested_fix: Use jnum() for these fields and add a per-state validity count for beam points instead of 0.

low.title: Stress histories are serialized with a hard-coded unit "MPa" regardless of deck units
low.mechanism: `stress_results_[i].unit = "MPa";` (409), also max_principal (421) and min_principal (426). partStatsToJSON writes it as-is: `oss << ind2 << "\"unit\": \"" << stats.unit` (AnalysisResult.hpp:508).
low.scenario: Real Test_Impact_A (a GPa-mm-ms deck): analysis_result.json stress_history[0] has unit "MPa" with global_max 0.08627328, which is actually 86 MPa. A Pa deck would carry 3e8 labeled MPa.
low.consumers: koo_impact_report/loader.py:1234 copies it into rec["stress_unit"] (not currently displayed, since the impact report uses _detect_unit_system). The deep report hard-codes 'MPa' in its HTML independently. Any external reader of analysis_result.json (the DynaForge export) would mislabel.
low.suggested_fix: Emit an empty unit or "deck_units" unless the unit system is actually detected (for example from the keyword file's *CONTROL_UNITS or the impact loader's detector).

low.title: max_element_id/min_element_id written as 0 for series that never set them
low.mechanism: timePointToJSON always writes `"max_element_id": tp.max_element_id, "min_element_id": tp.min_element_id` (491-492). SinglePassAnalyzer never sets min_element_id for eff_plastic_strain, vm_strain, σ1 or ε1 series, or max_element_id for σ3/ε3 series (SinglePassAnalyzer.cpp 771-797, 812-826). The default 0 goes out as an element ID.
low.scenario: Real Test_Impact_A stress/part_10_max_principal_stress.csv rows are `0.000001,0.040159,0.031681,0.035920,34004,0`, and the JSON has min_element_id 0 at every point of max_principal_history. 0 is not a valid LS-DYNA element ID.
low.consumers: No current Python consumer reads min_element_id (the sphere loader reads only Max_Element_ID; deep report peak_element_id uses the stress series' max_element_id), so the defect is latent.
low.suggested_fix: Track and write the IDs, or omit the key (or write null) for series where it is not tracked.

low.title: Max_Disp_Node_ID is internal 1-based node index, not the user node ID
low.mechanism: `max_node_id = static_cast<int32_t>(node_idx + 1);  // 1-based` is written to the 'Max_Disp_Node_ID' CSV column (unified_analyzer.cpp:93). mesh.real_node_ids exists but is not used.
low.scenario: /data/ball_drop_test_v7/ex01 deck node IDs are 1..338 and then jump to 1001. The CSV reports Max_Disp_Node_ID 1427 and 1317, which are actually real nodes 2089 and 1979. Nodes 1427 and 1317 also exist in the deck, so a user looking them up checks the wrong node.
low.consumers: motion/part_N_motion.csv (parsed into koo_deep_report MotionData.max_disp_node, documented as '최대 변위 노드 ID' in DATA_STRUCTURE.md). No report currently renders it.
low.suggested_fix: Map through mesh.real_node_ids[node_idx] when non-empty.

low.title: Extended JSON set_reports writes notes/name/title unescaped; a multi-line ffmpeg error makes analysis_result.json invalid
low.mechanism: `extra << "\"" << sr.notes[j] << "\"";` (also sr.name at :806 and sr.title at :809, which comes from the *SET title). metrics.json escapes these via jesc, but analysis_result.json does not. UnifiedAnalyzerSectionRender.cpp:306 pushes `"뷰 실패 [..]: " + err`, where err comes from SectionViewRenderer::assembleMp4:2196 `"ffmpeg failed (exit " + rc + "): " + ffout`, which contains raw newlines.
low.scenario: A set view whose ffmpeg encode fails, for example an odd width that libx264 rejects, or 'sh: 1: ffmpeg: not found'. The note contains '\n', and Python json.load raises 'Invalid control character' (verified). Every consumer of that folder's analysis_result.json fails to load the run.
low.consumers: Anything reading analysis_result.json in a folder that also has set_reports (see the shared-folder custom report finding): sphere, impact reuse, deep _parse_outputs
low.suggested_fix: Route all string fields in toExtendedJSON (motion/quality part_name, set name/title/notes, surface description/note) through escapeJSON.

low.title: element_quality min_jacobian written fixed(4): small negative Jacobians print as '-0.0000' and fail the `< 0` critical check
low.mechanism: `<< std::fixed << std::setprecision(4) << q.peak_aspect_ratio ... << ", \"min_jacobian\": " << q.min_jacobian`. deep html_report.py:1970 `q.min_jacobian < 0 ? 'crit' : (q.min_jacobian < 0.3 ? 'warn' : '')`.
low.scenario: A barely inverted element with scaled Jacobian -4e-5 is written as '-0.0000', parsed as -0.0, and `-0 < 0` is false. The cell is styled 'warn' instead of 'crit' and shows '-0.000'.
low.consumers: koo_deep_report element-quality table
low.suggested_fix: Use defaultfloat with setprecision(10) (the existing jnum helper) for the quality fields.

low.title: Time-series JSON (data points, global_max/min, time_of_max) uses fixed(8), so values below 5e-9 become 0
low.mechanism: timePointToJSON:485 `oss << std::fixed << std::setprecision(8)` and partStatsToJSON:512 `std::fixed << std::setprecision(8) << stats.globalMax()`. The file's own jnum comment (:692-697) documents this hazard for hotspot fields but not for histories. HEAD 63577f5 fixes it after 36ea5db.
low.scenario: Eff. plastic strain peak 3e-9 is written as 0.00000000, so strain_history global_max reads as 0 ('no plasticity'). Production Test_005 JSON strain entries are quantized to 1e-08 (e.g. min -1e-08).
low.consumers: koo_deep_report _parse_series (peak strain KPI), koo_impact_report _extract_part_stress_strain (peak_strain)
low.suggested_fix: Serialize with jnum (defaultfloat, setprecision(10)), as HEAD already does.

low.title: Principal and strain CSVs carry element ID 0 as if real in one ID column

refuted.defect_class: 2/5 downsampled range + wrong quantity + material index used as part ID
refuted.title: Per-part auto fringe range comes from von Mises on 5 sampled states, looks elements up by material index, and is applied whatever the fringe type
refuted.mechanism: `if (task.options.auto_fringe_range) { auto [fmin, fmax] = computePartFringeRange(reader, target_parts, total_states); if (fmax > 0.0) { task.options.auto_fringe_range = false; task.options.fringe_max = fmax; } }` does not check job.fringe_type. computePartFringeRange always computes von Mises, samples `k * (total_states - 1) / 4` (5 states), and selects elements with `target_set.count(mesh.solid_materials[i])` (l.74), i.e. internal material index compared with user part IDs.
refuted.scenario: (a) A render job with parts:[pid] and fringe eff_plastic_strain (koo_deep_report job_builder emits 'fringe': 'eff_plastic_strain' with 'parts' for target_part_ids / per-part renders) gets a fixed range of 0~σ_vm_max (e.g. 0~350 MPa) on a strain field of about 0.05, so the part renders in the minimum color. (b) On a 992-state run the samples are 0,247,495,743,991; a peak at state 130 exceeds fringe_max and the legend is clipped. (c) Where part IDs are not in material order (battery deck: material index 7→part 30, 9→part 100) the range is taken from a different part or none.
refuted.consumers: LSPrePost section-view MP4s in renders/, shown in the koo_deep_report render gallery; the legend max is the displayed number. LSPrePost rendering inside the SIF is currently blocked by known item (c), so the reach today is host-side rendering.
refuted.suggested_fix: Only override the range when fringe_type is von_mises (or compute the matching quantity). Scan all in-memory states instead of 5. Match on mesh.solid_parts/shell_parts (real part IDs), not *_materials.

verdicts.reason: The code in computePartFringeRange does have the flaws described: it always computes von Mises, it samples only 5 states, and it matches `mesh.solid_materials` (material indices) against user part IDs. But none of this ever reaches a render. computePartFringeRange only runs when `target_parts` is non-empty, and that same block first sets `task.options.highlight_parts`. Every task goes through renderAnimation, renderSectionView or renderImage, and all three end up in LSPrePostRenderer::generateScript. When `highlight_parts` is non-empty, generateScript takes the `has_target` branch, which writes `fringe <code>` and `pfringe` but no `range userdef`. The only place that writes `options.fringe_min` or `options.fringe_max` into the script is the `else` branch (no target parts), and that branch can never see the computed per-part range. Nothing else reads `task.options.fringe_min`, `fringe_max` or `auto_fringe_range`. The `fringe_max` at line 743 is an unrelated local pixel variable used for cropping. So LSPrePost always picks its own fringe range for per-part section renders. The legend cannot be forced to 0~σ_vm_max on a strain field, cannot be clipped by the 5-state sampling, and cannot take its range from the wrong part. The only visible effect is the log line "Per-part fringe range: 0 ~ X", which may show a von Mises value for the wrong part. That is console text, not report data.

The claim is refuted because the range this code computes never reaches the rendered video. The code at l.599 does have all three flaws the claim describes: it always computes von Mises, it samples only 5 states, and it matches parts by material index instead of real part ID. But `computePartFringeRange` only runs when `target_parts` is non-empty. Just before that call, l.591 always sets `task.options.highlight_parts = target_parts`. The renderer writes one script for images, animations and section views (`renderImage` → `generateScript`). That script writes `range userdef fringe_min fringe_max` only in the branch where `highlight_parts` is empty. When target parts exist, it takes the genselect branch, which writes `fringe N` / `pfringe` and no range command. So LSPrePost keeps its own automatic range. The forced `fringe_max` only ends up in the log line "Per-part fringe range: ...". Nothing else reads `task.options.fringe_max`: the `fringe_max` near l.743 is a local pixel size for cropping, and `part_section_renders` never calls this function. None of the three scenarios can change a rendered legend or colormap: (a) von Mises range on a strain fringe, (b) a peak between samples clipped from the legend, (c) the material-index/part-ID mismatch. The only visible effect is a misleading log line, which is cosmetic.

refuted.defect_class: silent fallback to 0 in a parsed series
refuted.title: Motion CSV parser turns non-finite or unparsable cells into 0.0, which then plots and ranks as a real zero displacement or velocity
refuted.mechanism: `try: v = float(row.get(key, 0) or 0) except ValueError: return 0.0 ... return v if math.isfinite(v) else 0.0`. This is applied to Time, Avg_Disp_*, Avg_Vel_Mag, Avg_Acc_Mag and Max_Disp_Mag, and a missing column also becomes all zeros. `max_disp_node` falls back to 0 on ValueError.
refuted.scenario: Eroded free nodes make the part average and max nan/inf from state k onward (the scenario the code comment names). All later samples become 0.0, so the displacement chart drops to 0 and looks like the part returned to its origin. peak_disp_mag ignores the post-erosion states, and a nan Time cell becomes t=0, which puts the point at the chart origin.
refuted.consumers: MotionData -> PartSummary.peak_disp/vel/acc -> report.html motion and Deep Dive charts and KPIs; result.json; batch report.
refuted.suggested_fix: Store None/NaN for non-finite values (JSON-serialize as null so Plotly shows a gap), exclude them from max(), and count or flag the affected states instead of writing 0.0.

verdicts.reason: The Python fallback exists, but the scenario in the claim can't happen. Its premise is that eroded free nodes make the part's average and max displacement nan/inf, which the CSV then carries. At 36ea5db the only writer of motion/part_N_motion.csv is writeMotionCSV in examples/unified_analyzer.cpp. It takes its data from MotionAnalyzer, which already skips non-finite nodes before averaging (computeAverageDisplacement) and before taking the max (computeMaxDisplacement). So Avg_Disp_*, Avg_Disp_Mag and Max_Disp_Mag are always finite. Avg_Vel and Avg_Acc are finite differences of that finite average, guarded by dt > 0. d3plot coordinates are float32, so the largest finite value (3.4e38) squared stays finite in double; checked by compiling a snippet. Time is state.time straight from the file. The header is fixed and always has all 15 columns, so the "missing column becomes all zeros" case can't happen with this writer either. In production, the non-finite -> 0.0 coercion in fv never runs, and no post-erosion state is turned into a fake zero. The only way left to reach the ValueError or empty-cell -> 0 path is a CSV cut off mid-row: a partial last line would read as a 0.0 sample. That needs unified_analyzer to be killed or run out of disk while writing at the very end. It is not the erosion mechanism claimed, and it is not a realistic input.

The claimed path cannot occur at 36ea5db. The parser at python/koo_deep_report/koo_deep_report/core/d3plot_reader.py:592-609 does turn nan, inf and unparsable cells into 0.0. But koo_deep_report only parses motion CSVs that the C++ binary from the same commit has just written: run_analysis calls _run_ua and then _parse_outputs, and there is no path that reuses old CSVs. That binary cannot write nan or inf here.

1. Commit 75ba278 added this Python coercion together with C++ changes. In src/analysis/MotionAnalyzer.cpp, computeAverageDisplacement and computeMaxDisplacement now skip any node whose displacement is not finite. So Avg_Disp_* and Max_Disp_Mag are always finite, even when elements erode.
2. Avg_Vel and Avg_Acc are differences of those finite averages, divided by dt only when dt > 0. With single-precision coordinates (at most 3.4e38) and dt = 1e-7, the largest possible value is about 1e59, still finite. Time comes straight from the d3plot state time.
3. The CSV header in writeMotionCSV has not changed since the first commit 8f9ea8c, so a column is never missing.
4. C++ writes nan, -nan, inf and -inf, and Python's float() reads all of them. So the ValueError branch needs a truly corrupt cell. If unified_analyzer crashes, _run_ua raises on the nonzero return code before any parsing happens.
5. --skip-existing skips the whole case (it checks result.json and a schema marker). It does not re-read CSVs.

The only remaining route is a stale motion CSV written by a binary older than 75ba278 and left in the same output folder. That is not a realistic production input.

A nearby silent zero is real but is a different defect in C++, not this parser: if every node of a part is non-finite, computeAverageDisplacement returns (0,0,0) because count == 0. computeMaxDisplacement likewise returns 0 with node id 0.

refuted.defect_class: 4 (non-finite sample turns the real peak into 0)
refuted.title: The impact motion CSV parser does not coerce inf/nan, so one non-finite sample makes peak_g inf, which _safe() emits as 0
refuted.mechanism: `fv`: `return float(row.get(k, 0) or 0)` accepts 'inf'/'nan'. `i_max = max(range(len(pm.acc_mag)), key=lambda i: pm.acc_mag[i])` selects the inf (or index 0 if acc_mag[0] is nan), and the payload `"g": _safe(r.peak_g)` maps inf to 0.0. koo_deep_report's _parse_motion_csv explicitly coerces non-finite values to 0 for eroded/diverged nodes; this parser does not.
refuted.scenario: Reproduced with a motion CSV whose rows have Avg_Acc_Mag 0, 5e6, inf (C++ ostream writes 'inf'/'-nan' for a diverged state): pm.peak_g=inf, payload g=0.0, and the real 5e6 peak is lost. The part and position then read as the safest instead of the worst.
refuted.consumers: payload results g, kpi worst/n_critical, part_motion summary, heatmaps, analyzer findings (print 'inf').
refuted.suggested_fix: Mirror deep_report: treat non-finite values as missing (skip, or NaN excluded from argmax) and record a load_issue instead of mapping to 0.

verdicts.reason: The Python side works as the claim says. If a CSV has 'inf', fv() keeps it, argmax picks it and _safe() turns it into 0.0. But the claimed trigger, the C++ writer printing inf or nan for Avg_Acc_Mag in a diverged state, cannot happen at 36ea5db. Since commit 75ba278 (2026-06-24, 222 commits earlier), MotionAnalyzer::computeAverageDisplacement skips any node whose displacement is inf or nan, so the average displacement is always finite. If every node is skipped, it returns (0,0,0). Velocity and acceleration are finite differences guarded by `dt > 0`, and unified_analyzer.cpp:65 is the only writer of part_*_motion.csv. Finite inputs cannot overflow a double here. I tried the worst case for a single-precision d3plot: a float32-max coordinate jump with the smallest float32 time step at t=1e-3 (1.16e-10 s). It gives an acceleration magnitude of 4.3e58, which is still finite. Reaching inf would need finite double-precision coordinates of about 1e300, which is not a realistic LS-DYNA output. So the current pipeline never feeds this parser a non-finite value. The only way left is the reuse path at loader.py:1080 reading old CSVs made by a binary older than 75ba278. That makes it a latent hardening gap (low), not a production defect for realistic current inputs.

The Python part of the claim is right, but the scenario can't happen with CSVs that the unified_analyzer at 36ea5db writes. `fv` in loader.py:1136-1140 does accept 'inf', and `_safe` (payload/common.py:32) does turn inf/nan into 0. But the claim assumes the C++ writer outputs 'inf'/'-nan' in Avg_Acc_Mag when a state diverges, and at 36ea5db it doesn't.

1. Avg_Acc_Mag is set in only one place, MotionAnalyzer.cpp:281. Before any sum, `computeAverageDisplacement` skips every node whose dx/dy/dz is not finite (inf or nan).
2. If no node is left, count stays 0 and the average is (0,0,0), so no 0/0 happens.
3. Velocity and acceleration are only divided by dt under `dt > 0`. That check is false for dt = NaN, so a NaN time also produces no division.
4. With finite inputs, the result can only become non-finite by overflow. Single-precision d3plot values are at most 3.4e38. Even with dt = 7e-15 (the smallest float32 time step near 1e-7), acc is about 2.7e67 and its magnitude is still finite. Getting inf would need coordinates above about 1e140 from a double-precision d3plot, which a real run does not produce.

These guards came in with 75ba278 (2026-06-24, "exclude eroded free-node inf/nan from displacement"), which is an ancestor of 36ea5db. Its commit message says the C++ skip was added so newly written data is clean. So production runs of deep, impact or sphere, which make the motion CSVs with this binary, give finite Avg_Acc_Mag.

The only way to hit this is to reuse an old deep_report output folder made by a binary older than 75ba278, or to use a hand-written CSV. What's left is a missing second guard in Python compared with deep_report's `_parse_motion_csv`, which is at most a low-severity, latent gap.
